name: Balanced z0/z1 causal-bank sampling (BCS) -- fifth crossover-preservation attempt
authority: PI, 2026-09-04, choosing 'one more attempt: balanced bank' after CCP-S2, RSCFT, trunk-freeze, and SAC-RFT all failed the primary crossover gate. This is a fresh authorization, not covered by the earlier RSCFT-termination-rule override (which was spent by trunk-freeze) or by SAC_RFT_SPEC.json's own activation (spent by SAC-RFT).

NOT_A_NEW_HYPOTHESIS.note: this mechanism was identified and logged BEFORE CCP-S2 ever launched, specifically so it could not become a post-hoc explanation: CCP_S2_TREATMENT_RESULT.json#launch_manifest.documented_treatment_asymmetry_not_corrected, written 2026-09-03T04:22:29Z, before any CCP-S2 training step.

verbatim_prelaunch_caveat.implication_if_outcome_is_asymmetric: a pre-existing 3.5x z0/z1 imbalance in behaviour-changing supervision is already on record as a candidate explanation for a delta_A > 0, delta_B <= 0 outcome -- to be investigated, never assumed

NOT_A_NEW_HYPOTHESIS.why_investigating_it_now_is_not_p_hackin: the caveat predates all four outcomes it might explain (CCP-S2, RSCFT, trunk-freeze, SAC-RFT), was logged with the explicit intent of being tested later rather than assumed, and this spec is frozen before this experiment's own training run starts -- the same boundary every prior stage in this program has protected.

MECHANISM_CONFIRMED_BEFORE_FREEZING_THIS.nonzero_segments_rolled_out: 5 of 100 candidate segments passed CCP-S2's strictly-positive-over-both routing gate
MECHANISM_CONFIRMED_BEFORE_FREEZING_THIS.segment_composition: 3 segments tagged latent=0 (rows 214+123+116=453), 2 segments tagged latent=1 (rows 229+90=319) -- confirmed by reading CCP_S2_CAUSAL_BANK_ARRAY.json#segments directly, not inferred
MECHANISM_CONFIRMED_BEFORE_FREEZING_THIS.sampling_code_confirmed: rl/causal_sequence_runner.py:CausalSequenceRunner.step() draws batch_rows indices via torch.randint(0, self.n_rows, ...) -- UNIFORM over all 772 rows, no stratification by z_idx. The ~59/41 z0/z1 exposure ratio measured in every one of the four prior training runs (CCP-S2, RSCFT, trunk-freeze, SAC-RFT -- all reused this identical bank and this identical unmodified sampler) is a direct, mechanical consequence of this uniform draw over an already-imbalanced row pool, not a separate bug.
MECHANISM_CONFIRMED_BEFORE_FREEZING_THIS.what_this_experiment_changes: ONLY the sampling procedure. Same bank, same 5 segments, same routing, same segment weights, same loss function, same lambda/cadence/batch_rows. rl/causal_sequence_runner.py:BalancedCausalSequenceRunner (new, additive subclass -- CausalSequenceRunner itself is untouched, so every prior arm's code path remains exactly reproducible) pre-partitions bank rows by z_idx and draws an EQUAL count from each latent's own pool every step, guaranteeing exact per-step balance regardless of the 453/319 underlying skew.
MECHANISM_CONFIRMED_BEFORE_FREEZING_THIS.what_this_experiment_does_NOT_change: segment DIVERSITY. There are still only 3 distinct z0 segments and 2 distinct z1 segments. Balancing exposure COUNT means revisiting that same small pool more evenly; it does not enlarge it. If the true bottleneck is insufficient z1 supervision diversity (not merely under-sampling of the z1 rows that already exist), this experiment will not fix it -- that would require re-collecting Stage A/B data, explicitly out of scope given the deadline. This limitation is disclosed here, before the run, not discovered after a FAIL.

unchanged: warm-start checkpoint (original incumbent, final_ccp_successor_production.zip, where delta_A = +0.0938)

Stage A/B causal bank contents and routing

500k additional steps (matched horizon to every prior stage for comparability)

MECHANICAL_PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED_BEFORE_ANY: BalancedCausalSequenceRunner.self_test(): after 8 real steps against the real bank and a real trainer, gained z0/z1 exposure counts match the exact target split (24/24 per step x 8 = 192/192), not merely balanced on average

CausalSequenceRunner (parent, used by CONTROL) reproduces its historically-measured imbalance under the same real bank -- a contrast/positive-control check confirming the two classes genuinely differ in behavior, not just in name
both classes produce nonzero gradients through causal_supervision_loss (loss.backward() moves real parameters)
segment_bank_hash freshly rebuilt and verified against CCP_S2_CAUSAL_BANK_ARRAY.json before either class loads the npz

PRIMARY_GATE.criterion: delta_A > 0 AND LCB95(delta_A) > 0 AND delta_B > 0 AND LCB95(delta_B) > 0
PRIMARY_GATE.rule: same primary gate as every prior stage. No mercy, no reinterpretation.

ATTRIBUTION.statistic: preregistered PAIRED bootstrap over the shared 64 seeds, n_boot=20000, alpha=0.05, rng_seed=7

PREREGISTERED_INTERPRETATION.reading: balanced sampling recovered crossover where unbalanced sampling did not -- supports the supervision-imbalance hypothesis
crossover recovered under both; balancing not necessary under this run

balanced sampling also insufficient -- the bottleneck is more likely segment diversity (only 3 vs 2 distinct segments) than sampling weight, or the erosion mechanism is unrelated to the causal bank at all

EVAL_PROTOCOL.tie_or_reversal: any tie or reversal triggers a row-level integrity audit before interpretation, written before its rows are read -- same standard as every prior stage

PROGRAM_TERMINATION_RULE.this_is_the_attempt_the_new_evidence_jus: this experiment operationalizes a mechanism that was on record before any of the four prior FAILs and was explicitly deferred ('to be investigated, never assumed') rather than invented after seeing them. If BALANCED_TREATMENT also fails the primary gate, the honest reading is that supervision-COUNT imbalance was not the dominant erosion mechanism (segment diversity, or something outside the causal bank entirely, remains open) -- and per the deadline reality (Sept 15, 4v4/6v6 locked and required regardless of this outcome), a further architecture attempt at 2v2 crossover requires a fresh, explicit PI authorization the same way this one did, not an assumed continuation.
